prompt: ffmpeg ffmetadata chapter missing timebase assumed units
answer:
In current FFmpeg documentation, if a chapter’s `TIMEBASE` is omitted, `START` and `END` are interpreted as **nanoseconds**.

```ini
[CHAPTER]
START=0
END=60000000000
title=Chapter 1
```

This represents a chapter from 0 to 60 seconds. To use another unit, specify the timebase explicitly:

```ini
[CHAPTER]
TIMEBASE=1/1000
START=0
END=60000
title=Chapter 1
```

Here, the values are in milliseconds. (FFmpeg Formats Documentation: https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html)
